title: Contrast claim is overstated: informational text rendered in the --sr-text-disabled token sits at 2.3–2.6:1 in both themes
description: ACCESSIBILITY.md claims body text and primary interface text meet 4.5:1 in both themes, with exactly one disclosed exception (percentage labels inside chart bars). In fact, real informational text — not disabled controls — is rendered in --sr-text-disabled, which computes to 2.56:1 light (#A1A1AA on #FFFFFF) / 2.45:1 on the page bg, and 2.29:1 dark (#52525B on #18181B). Locations: Checklists.tsx:177 and :668 (the result-count labels that are also the polite live regions), MediaCommentsSection.tsx:100 and NamedBirdsTable.tsx:77 (count labels), SpeciesDetail.tsx:461 ('{n} species' count) and :584 (scientific names inside the species-combobox options), ChecklistComparer.tsx:534 (italic placeholder labels), and the uppercase mini-headers in SetupRequired.tsx:56, ListComparer.tsx:203, HelpDocs.tsx:354. None of these are covered by the statement's disclosed chart-label exception, so the published claim is false as written, and low-vision users genuinely cannot read these labels.
fix: Use --sr-text-muted (4.83:1 light / 6.91:1 dark — already passing) for all informational text and reserve --sr-text-disabled strictly for genuinely disabled controls; or add a passing 'faint text' token. Then re-verify the ACCESSIBILITY.md contrast paragraph.

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran WCAG luminance math: --sr-text-disabled is 2.56:1 on white / 2.46:1 on --sr-surface-faint (the line 177/668 labels' actual backdrop) light, 2.29:1 / 2.20:1 dark — all well below 4.5:1 for 11-12px informational text. All ten cited locations exist and use the token for real content (count labels that are also the only result-count display, combobox sci names, mini-headers), and ACCESSIBILITY.md's sole disclosed exception (chart-bar percentage labels) covers none of them, so the published AA claim is false as written. Fix is correct and convention-compliant: --sr-text-muted passes in both themes (4.83/4.63 light, 6.91/6.63 dark) and is already defined in both.

title: Help overlay: fixed 200px TOC sidebar never collapses — content column collapses to ~30px at 320px width
description: The HelpDocs body lays the TOC and content side by side with inline styles only — no media query and no wrap. The TOC is `width: 200, flexShrink: 0`, the row adds `padding: '0 24px'` and `gap: 40`, so at a 320 CSS px viewport (e.g. 1280px window at 400% zoom, or a phone) the help content column gets roughly 320 − 48 − 200 − 40 ≈ 32px. Markdown text wraps at one or two characters per line (long words overflow), making the in-app documentation effectively unreadable exactly for the low-vision users most likely to need it. Every other layout in the app handles this (globals.css has a 640px media query; TabNav measures and collapses), so this is the one true reflow failure found. It also contradicts ACCESSIBILITY.md line 39 ("The layout reflows for narrow windows and at large sizes … without clipping content").
fix: Below a narrow-width breakpoint (~700px), stack the TOC above the content (flexDirection column) or move it behind a disclosure button. A `.sr-help-body` class plus a rule in the existing `@media (max-width: 640px)` block in globals.css is the smallest change; alternatively reuse the TabNav measurement pattern.

verdict.reasoning: HelpDocs.tsx lines 341-351 lay out the TOC (inline width:200, flexShrink:0) and content (flex:1, minWidth:0) with gap 40 and 0 24px padding, all inline styles with no className, and globals.css's only width media block (640px) has no help-overlay rules — so at 320 CSS px the content column is ~32px as claimed. ACCESSIBILITY.md line 39 affirmatively claims reflow works (exempting only tables/maps), so this is contradicted rather than disclosed. Severity serious is fair: the in-app documentation becomes unreadable at 400% zoom for exactly the low-vision users it serves.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested .sr-help-body class + rule in the existing @media (max-width: 640px) block is right, but because the layout is inline styles the override needs !important (the existing block already does this pattern for .sr-header's inline padding) — e.g. add classes to the row and nav and rule `.sr-help-row { flex-direction: column !important; gap: 0 !important; } .sr-help-toc { width: 100% !important; position: static !important; max-height: none !important; }`. The existing 640px breakpoint is sufficient for SC 1.4.10 (failure threshold is 320 CSS px); no new ~700px breakpoint needed.

title: Selected state not programmatically exposed on segmented controls and toggle pills
description: The shared SegControl renders plain <button>s whose active option is conveyed only by background/border/font-weight — no aria-pressed, aria-checked, or radiogroup semantics. It is used for the Map Explorer radius (MapExplorer.tsx:700), breeding filter (:881), Pins/Heatmap display mode (:912), and All/Week (:1285). The same style-only-state defect appears in SpeciesDetail.tsx:1189 (Pins/Heatmap map-mode buttons), BirdingStats.tsx:541 (accumulation granularity), :1628 (breeding filter pills), :1717 (media view mode), ListComparer.tsx:215 (My List / Upload source buttons), and MapExplorer.tsx:1030 (hotspot kind-legend toggles, whose only state cue is opacity 0.4). A screen-reader user cannot tell which option is active. This directly contradicts ACCESSIBILITY.md: "Filter pills announce whether they are pressed." The codebase already has the correct pattern (SortSeg in Checklists.tsx:74, SnowMap.tsx:144, SpeciesDetail graph groups :962/:974).
fix: Add aria-pressed={value === opt.value} (or role="radio"/aria-checked inside a role="radiogroup") to SegControl's buttons and to each listed location; wrap each group in role="group" with an aria-label.

verdict.reasoning: SegControl (MapSidebarUI.tsx:15-29) renders plain buttons with style-only active state, and every cited usage checks out: MapExplorer 700/881/912/1285, SpeciesDetail ~1189, BirdingStats 541/1628/1717, ListComparer 215, and the hotspot kind-legend toggles at MapExplorer 1030 whose only state cue is opacity 0.4. The correct pattern does exist in SortSeg (Checklists.tsx, role=group + aria-pressed) and SnowMap.tsx:144, and ACCESSIBILITY.md's 'filter pills announce whether they are pressed' claim is contradicted rather than disclosed as an exception. Serious is fair: a screen-reader user cannot determine the active option on roughly ten primary filter/view controls.
verdict.fixNote: Give SegControl an ariaLabel prop rendered as role="group" aria-label on its wrapper div plus aria-pressed={value === opt.value} on each button, mirroring SortSeg in Checklists.tsx (the SidebarLabel above it is not programmatically associated, so the group needs its own label). Apply the same aria-pressed to the inline groups in SpeciesDetail, BirdingStats, and ListComparer; for the kind-legend visibility toggles use aria-pressed={!isHidden} so pressed means shown.

title: Media Targets keyboard path is partial and ACCESSIBILITY.md overstates it
description: Media Target chips are DOM <Marker>s with a click-only <div> (no tabindex/role), so the chips themselves are not operable by keyboard. The only keyboard route to a target popup is the 'Nearest Targets' list (MapExplorer.tsx:1292-1338), which is hard-capped at 10 items sorted by distance from the SEARCH CENTER (nearest10 useMemo, MapExplorer.tsx:453-461) — it is not scoped to the map viewport, does not update on pan/zoom, and shows no over-cap hint. Any target beyond the nearest 10 (easy with a 25-50 mi radius) has no keyboard path at all. ACCESSIBILITY.md line 13 claims "The Media Targets mode's 'Nearest Targets' list works the same way" and that "These lists are scoped to the current map view and update as you pan or zoom" — that is true for sightings/hotspots (cap 200, BoundsTracker-driven) but false for targets, so the published statement is currently inaccurate.
fix: Render an InViewMarkerList for targets like the other two modes (items = locationGroups filtered by mapBounds via markersInView, cap 200 with the over-cap hint), keeping 'Nearest Targets' as a convenience list; or at minimum correct ACCESSIBILITY.md to say the targets list is the nearest 10 from the search center, not viewport-scoped.

verdict.reasoning: Verified TargetMarkers.tsx:69-75: chips are click-only divs with no tabindex/role, and MapExplorer.tsx:453-461 confirms nearest10 is distance-from-search-center, slice(0,10), with no mapBounds dependency — so targets beyond the nearest 10 have no keyboard route at all, unlike sightings/hotspots which use markersInView (cap 200, viewport-driven) into InViewMarkerList. ACCESSIBILITY.md line 13's claim that the targets list 'works the same way' and is 'scoped to the current map view' is factually wrong for this mode. Genuine 2.1.1 Level A gap in a primary feature plus an inaccurate published statement; serious stands.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested InViewMarkerList fix is correct and matches existing conventions, with two precisions: (1) the locId grouping currently lives in TargetMarkers.tsx's locationGroups useMemo, so either lift it to MapExplorer (shared with displayedTargetPins) or recompute it there before feeding markersInView, and wire onActivate to the existing setSelectedTargetLocId + setPanTarget pair (same owner the chip click uses); (2) per CLAUDE.md, update ACCESSIBILITY.md in the same change — either to truthfully describe the viewport-scoped list once built, or immediately to state that the targets list is the nearest 10 from the search center.

title: Mobile filter sidebar: Escape focus-restore is dead code, trap snapshot goes stale, other close paths drop focus — published a11y claim is false
wcag: 2.4.3 Focus Order A (and 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap A integrity)
description: Three defects in the one focus trap the app ships: (1) The Escape handler runs `setSidebarOpen(false); filtersButtonRef.current?.focus()` (lines 200-203), but the Filters button is inside the FAB cluster rendered only when the sidebar is CLOSED (`{!sidebarOpen && (<div className="sr-map-fab-cluster">` at line 1446, ref at 1461). While the sidebar is open the ref is null, so the restore is a no-op; the focused element then gets display:none (`.sr-map-sidebar-hidden`) and the browser dumps focus to <body> — the keyboard user restarts from the top of the document. ACCESSIBILITY.md line 51 explicitly claims 'Escape closes it and returns focus to the button that opened it' — that claim is currently false. (2) The focusable list is snapshotted once at open (lines 192-196: `sidebar.querySelectorAll(...)`, then `first`/`last` captured); the sidebar contains a Filters accordion and async-loaded hotspot/target lists, so after content changes Tab escapes the trap into obscured background content (the page behind is not inert). (3) The mobile 'Close filters' button (line 1414) and the backdrop click (line 1400) close via `setSidebarOpen(false)` with no focus restore — same display:none → body drop.
fix: Keep the FAB cluster mounted while the sidebar is open (hide it with CSS/inert) so the ref survives, or restore focus in an effect that runs after sidebarOpen flips to false. Re-query focusables on each Tab keydown (HelpDocs.tsx:258-273 already does this correctly — reuse that pattern). Route ALL close paths (Escape, Close button, backdrop) through one close() that restores focus.

verdict.reasoning: All three defects verified: (1) the FAB cluster with filtersButtonRef renders only when !sidebarOpen (line 1446, ref 1461), so the Escape handler's focus() at line 202 runs while ref.current is null — dead code — and globals.css confirms .sr-map-sidebar-hidden is display:none on mobile, dropping focus to body; ACCESSIBILITY.md line 51's claim is therefore false. (2) Focusables are snapshotted once (lines 192-196) with [sidebarOpen]-only deps while the sidebar content is dynamic. (3) The Close button (1414) and backdrop (1400) close with no restore. Serious is appropriate: every keyboard close path on mobile strands focus, and the published a11y statement affirms the broken behavior.

title: Species Detail / Named Birds map pins (DOM markers) have no keyboard access path
description: The shared SightingsMap renders each sighting pin as a react-map-gl <Marker> whose content is a plain <div> with a click handler routed through Marker onClick — no tabIndex, no role, no keydown handler — so a keyboard user can never open the per-coordinate popup. On Species Detail ("Sighting Locations" map) that popup is the ONLY place exposing the per-sighting checklist links for sightings without comments (Top Locations rows at SpeciesDetail.tsx:1122-1137 show only name+count; the Comments section only covers commented sightings), so those eBird links are pointer-only functionality. Same pattern, lower impact (keyboard equivalents exist nearby): TargetMarkers.tsx:69-74 chip markers (mitigated by the sidebar "Nearest Targets" locate buttons opening the same popup) and BirdingStats.tsx:863-872 geographic-stats rank pins (popup content fully duplicated in the adjacent "Top locations" text lists). Named Birds card maps are also unreachable but each row already lists every sighting's checklist link (NamedBirdRow.tsx:90-100). Note ACCESSIBILITY.md's keyboard-alternative claim covers only the Map Explorer GL markers; these DOM-marker maps have no equivalent of its in-view lists.
fix: DOM markers CAN be focusable (unlike the GL pins): make the marker content a <button aria-label={locName + ' — N sightings'}> so Tab+Enter opens the popup, or reuse the Map Explorer pattern (a focusable list of coordinates that drives the same selectedCoord state). For Species Detail specifically, alternatively surface the per-coordinate checklist links in the keyboard-reachable Top Locations rows.

verdict.reasoning: Verified SightingsMap.tsx:54-58 (and TargetMarkers.tsx, BirdingStats.tsx:862-872): pins are plain div Marker children with click wired through react-map-gl's native click listener; maplibre only adds tabindex/keypress via setPopup(), which this code never uses, so no pin is focusable or keyboard-activatable. The Species Detail impact claim checks out — Top Locations rows (SpeciesDetail.tsx:1115-1138) show name+count only and the Comments section filters to commented sightings (line 372), so checklist links for uncommented sightings are popup-only, i.e. pointer-only. ACCESSIBILITY.md's keyboard-alternative claim is explicitly Map Explorer-scoped and its only disclosed exception is chart-label contrast, so this Level A lockout is undisclosed; serious is the right severity.
verdict.fixNote: The button-child fix needs no custom keydown handler: react-map-gl attaches a native click listener to the marker wrapper, so Enter/Space on a real <button aria-label={`${locName ?? coord}, ${n} sightings`}> child dispatches a click that bubbles to it. One refinement: maplibre's Marker.addTo() already stamps the wrapper div with role='button' + generic aria-label='Map marker', so via the Marker ref call marker.getElement().setAttribute('role','presentation') and removeAttribute('aria-label') to avoid a nested-button announcement (or instead set the descriptive aria-label + tabindex on the wrapper itself through the ref and skip the inner button). Apply the same treatment to TargetMarkers.tsx and the BirdingStats rank pins; the Species Detail alternative (links in Top Locations rows) should reuse the existing NamedBirdRow.tsx aria-label pattern for checklist anchors.

title: ACCESSIBILITY.md contrast claim is broader than the computed reality
description: The published statement says text, buttons, links, map popups and form controls 'meet the WCAG 2.1 AA contrast standard (4.5:1) in both the light and dark themes', with chart-bar labels as the only known exception. Computed counterexamples outside that exception: light-theme active pills/links on tinted backgrounds 4.03–4.41:1 (accent-on-accent-bg, error-on-error-bg, active tab on page bg), --sr-text-disabled used on content at 2.29–2.56:1, dark-theme target chips at 1.52–1.92:1, dark-theme breeding pills at 1.97–2.94:1, and form-control borders at 1.19–1.27:1 (non-text). The repo treats this file as a published statement whose claims must be true; today it overstates. (Verified-true parts: the tier-1 badge example, the recency-dot hidden labels, the text-footer/sci-name token fixes, focus-ring contrast, and the dark-mode popup theming.)
fix: Either fix the token-level failures in this report (most are 1-line token edits) and keep the claim, or temporarily widen the known-exceptions paragraph to honestly cover active-state tints in light theme and chip/pill labels in dark theme.

verdict.reasoning: Recomputed all cited ratios independently and each one holds with co-occurring real UI: light accent-on-accent-bg 4.03 / error-on-error-bg 4.41 (LifeList.tsx:107-108 active pills) / active tab on bg 4.32 (TabNav.tsx:94); --sr-text-disabled 2.29-2.57 on non-disabled content (Settings.tsx:240/376 sublabels); dark target chips 1.52/1.92 (white text hardcoded in lib/mapExplorerFormat.ts:61-62); dark breeding pills 1.97-2.94 after alpha-blending the 0.08 tints (BreedingCodeList.tsx:43-60); borders 1.19-1.27. ACCESSIBILITY.md:31 claims AA in both themes with only the chart-bar-label exception, so the published statement is overstated — and CLAUDE.md explicitly requires this file's claims to stay true. The only stated exception does not cover any of these, so alreadyDisclosed is false.
verdict.fixNote: The two-option fix is sound, with one correction: the dark-theme target-chip failure is not a token edit — lib/mapExplorerFormat.ts hardcodes text: 'white' (itself against the no-hardcoded-colors convention). Fix it like the existing old-tier pattern: add --sr-map-target-fresh-text / --sr-map-target-mid-text tokens to BOTH :root and [data-theme="dark"] in globals.css and reference them, mirroring --sr-map-target-old-text. The breeding-pill fix likewise needs the dark-theme tier text colors lightened (or pill text switched to --sr-text) rather than tint-alpha tweaks, since the 0.08 tint barely moves the blended background. Any token change must land in both theme blocks per convention; ACCESSIBILITY.md edits alone need no version bump.

title: Map chrome text inherits MapLibre's fixed `font: 12px/20px Helvetica` — does not scale with the in-app Text Size control
description:
maplibre-gl.css (imported at SnowMap.tsx:7) sets `.maplibregl-map{font:12px/20px Helvetica Neue,…}`. The app's `.maplibregl-popup-content` override in globals.css:568 themes colors but sets no font-size or family, so any map-rendered text without an explicit rem size stays at a hard 12px Helvetica regardless of the Text Size setting. Affected: (1) the AtlasLayer block popup title — `
{sel.name}
` at AtlasLayer.tsx:213 and the linked variant at :208-211 have no fontSize; (2) the attribution credits on every map (SnowMap.tsx:121 `attributionControl={{ compact: true }}` — provider links render at fixed 12px when expanded); (3) the AtlasLayer popup's default close button (it is the only popup that doesn't pass `closeButton={false}`, so users get maplibre's small fixed-size '×' — also a WCAG 2.2 2.5.8 Target Size concern). This matters more here than in a typical web app: ACCESSIBILITY.md:37 states the Text Size control is "especially useful in the desktop app, which has no browser zoom of its own", so on desktop this text is genuinely un-resizable. All other popups (SightingMarkers, HotspotMarkers, TargetMarkers, SightingsMap, the BirdingStats geo popup) set explicit rem sizes and are fine.
fix: In globals.css extend the existing popup override: `.maplibregl-popup-content { font-size: 0.8125rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); }` and add `.maplibregl-ctrl-attrib { font-size: 0.6875rem; }`; give the AtlasLayer block-name elements an explicit rem fontSize; pass `closeButton={false}` on the AtlasLayer popup for consistency with the other four popups (its onClose path already exists).

verdict.reasoning: Every claim checks out: maplibre-gl.css sets .maplibregl-map{font:12px/20px Helvetica Neue,...}, the globals.css:568 popup override adds no font-size/family, the AtlasLayer block name (:208-213) has no fontSize, .maplibregl-ctrl-attrib inherits the fixed 12px, and the Text Size control scales only rem text via html{font-size:calc(100% * var(--sr-text-scale))} (globals.css:378). On desktop — which ACCESSIBILITY.md:37 itself says has no browser zoom — this text is un-resizable, a genuine 1.4.4 failure there (web is saved by browser zoom); at 200% the popup title would render smaller than its own muted secondary text. AtlasLayer is indeed the only popup of six without closeButton={false}, but that part of the fix is wrong (see fixNote).
verdict.fixNote: The CSS parts are right: extend the existing globals.css override with `.maplibregl-popup-content { font-size: 0.8125rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); }` and add `.maplibregl-ctrl-attrib { font-size: 0.6875rem; }`, and give the AtlasLayer block-name elements an explicit rem fontSize (e.g. 0.8125rem). But do NOT pass closeButton={false} on the AtlasLayer popup: it also sets closeOnClick={false}, so the default close button is its only dismiss affordance and its only keyboard-operable control — removing it would strand the popup open and worsen 2.1.1. Instead keep the button and size it via the existing .maplibregl-popup-close-button override (e.g. add `font-size: 1rem; padding: 2px 8px;`), which also addresses the 2.5.8 target-size concern.

title: Chart hover tooltips are not hoverable (1.4.13): cursor-following wrapper with pointer-events none on all five recharts Tooltip mounts
wcag: 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus AA (failure F95 — content on hover not hoverable)
description: All five recharts <Tooltip> mounts — BirdingStats.tsx:575 and :601 (life-list accumulation area charts), :1276 (checklists-by-observer bar chart), :1768 (media-over-time line chart), and MediaStatsSections.tsx:320 (media-by-hour stacked bar chart) — pass only contentStyle/formatter/labelFormatter, so recharts 3.8.1 defaults apply (trigger 'hover', no fixed position, no wrapperStyle). The library renders the tooltip in a wrapper hardcoded to pointerEvents:'none' that follows the cursor at a ~10px offset (node_modules/recharts/es6/component/TooltipBoundingBox.js:77), so the pointer can never be moved over the tooltip content: approaching it repositions the box and swaps its data to a different point, and at the plot edge the move exits the hover area and the tooltip vanishes. That fails 1.4.13's hoverable condition, which exists for screen-magnification users who must bring revealed content under the lens to read it — the media chart's five-line tooltip in particular can extend past a 400% lens and cannot be panned to without the content changing. The other two 1.4.13 conditions PASS in this recharts version (verified in installed source, see passes), which bounds the severity, as does the trigger-adjacent placement; and because every chart wrapper is role="img" with an aria-label summary, this is a sighted-pointer-user issue only (per-point values are otherwise unavailable as visible text anywhere in the UI). The tooltip is also clamped inside the chart viewBox (allowEscapeViewBox default false), so it can overlay bars, axis ticks, and the media chart's in-container legend — acceptable under 1.4.13 only because the Escape dismissal works. ACCESSIBILITY.md makes no claim about hover content, so this is an undisclosed gap rather than a false statement.
evidence: BirdingStats.tsx:575-582/:601-605/:1276-1280/:1768-1773 and MediaStatsSections.tsx:320-323 pass no content/trigger/position/wrapperStyle props; recharts 3.8.1 TooltipBoundingBox.js:77 sets `pointerEvents: 'none'` in positionStyle and translates the box from the live cursor coordinate via getTooltipTranslate; defaultTooltipProps in Tooltip.js:36-58 sets `trigger: 'hover'`.
suggestedFix: Pick one per-chart approach and apply it to all five mounts: (a) anchor the tooltip with a fixed `position={{ x, y }}` (e.g. a chart corner) plus `wrapperStyle={{ pointerEvents: 'auto' }}` — wrapperStyle is spread after the hardcoded style so it wins — making the box stationary and physically hoverable; or (b) switch to `trigger="click"` (supported in recharts 3), which makes the content activation-triggered and exempt from 1.4.13 entirely, matching the posture the app already takes for map popups; or (c) surface the per-point values in a visible-text alternative (a small data-table disclosure under each chart). Mention chart tooltips in ACCESSIBILITY.md once fixed.

verdict.reasoning: All five Tooltip mounts (BirdingStats.tsx:575/601/1276/1768, MediaStatsSections.tsx:320) pass only contentStyle/formatter/labelFormatter, and the installed recharts 3.8.1 hardcodes pointerEvents:'none' plus cursor-following translate in TooltipBoundingBox.js and trigger:'hover' in defaultTooltipProps — so the hover content can never be hovered, an F95 failure of 1.4.13. The bounding claims also check out: Escape dismissal exists in TooltipBoundingBox, every chart wrapper is role=img with an aria-label, and wrapperStyle is spread after the hardcoded positionStyle so fix option (a) works. No existing finding covers 1.4.13/chart tooltips and ACCESSIBILITY.md says nothing about hover content.
verdict.fixNote: Option (a) is verified workable in the installed source: outerStyle = {...positionStyle, visibility..., ...props.wrapperStyle}, so wrapperStyle={{ pointerEvents: 'auto' }} wins, but it only satisfies 1.4.13 combined with a fixed position prop (otherwise the box still tracks the cursor). Option (b) trigger="click" is the lowest-risk route and matches the app's map-popup posture.

title: Disclosed chart-bar-label exception verified — but it understates the dark-theme failures (down to 1.29:1) and a working fix already exists in-code
description: ACCESSIBILITY.md's known exception ('a few dense data-visualization labels (percentage figures printed inside saturated chart bars) do not yet meet AA in every case') is accurate in direction but materially understates scope. Computed: LIGHT — white on --sr-graph-audio 2.15:1 (protocol bar), white on --sr-chart-slate 2.56:1, white on --sr-graph-photo 3.68:1, white on --sr-graph-video 4.23:1. DARK — --sr-text on --sr-chart-blue-light 1.29:1 (comment/species-notes bars, BirdingStats.tsx:1384/1405), white on graph-audio 1.44:1, white on --sr-accent 1.92:1 (hardcoded '#fff' at protocol bar :1181), white on graph-photo 2.54:1, white on chart-slate 2.56:1, --sr-text on chart-slate 2.33:1 (:1361), white on chart-blue-dark 3.68:1 (:1125). In dark mode it is most in-bar labels, not 'a few'. Notably, line 1358 already uses var(--sr-on-accent) which passes in BOTH themes (4.52/7.75) — the failures are the literal '#fff' and var(--sr-text) usages that don't adapt.
fix: Replace literal '#fff' bar-label colors with per-fill adaptive tokens (the existing --sr-on-accent pattern), or render the percentage outside/beside the segment when the segment color can't carry AA text; then tighten the ACCESSIBILITY.md wording to match whatever remains.

verdict.reasoning: Independently recomputed every cited pair with my own WCAG relative-luminance implementation; all match (dark --sr-text on --sr-chart-blue-light = 1.29:1 at lines 1384/1405, white on dark graph-audio 1.44, white on dark accent 1.92 via the hardcoded '#fff' at 1181, dark text-on-slate 2.33 at 1361, white on dark chart-blue-dark 3.68 at 1125), and line 1358's --sr-on-accent does pass both themes (4.52/7.75) proving the fix pattern exists in-code. Labels are 11-12px weight-600, so the 4.5:1 normal-text threshold applies — in dark mode most in-bar labels fail, some catastrophically, which materially exceeds the 'a few cases' wording in ACCESSIBILITY.md line 31. Confirmed at moderate: the percentages are supplemental (raw counts appear in the adjacent header text), but 1.29:1 is effectively invisible text.

title: Missing-media type icons in Media Targets popup and marker chips have no text alternative anywhere
description: The whole point of a media target is which media types (photo/audio/video) the user is missing, but that information is conveyed exclusively by unnamed inline SVGs: in the target popup (TargetMarkers.tsx:91-97, bare <svg> per missing type, no aria-hidden, no label), in the on-map chip labels (TargetMarkers.tsx:62, MEDIA_ICONS SVG strings injected via dangerouslySetInnerHTML), and the keyboard-accessible "Nearest Targets" sidebar rows (MapExplorer.tsx:~1315-1318) show only name/location/distance — they omit missing types entirely. A screen-reader user can find a target but never learn which media it is missing. This also weakens the ACCESSIBILITY.md claim that icon-only information "carries a hidden text label so it is never lost to a screen reader."
fix: In the popup, give each type span role="img" aria-label={`Missing ${t.toLowerCase()}`} (or append sr-only text) and aria-hidden the SVGs; add the missing types as text (visible or sr-only) to the Nearest Targets sidebar rows so the keyboard/SR path carries the full information.

verdict.reasoning: Verified all three cited surfaces: popup spans (TargetMarkers.tsx:91-97) hold bare unnamed SVGs with no role/aria-label/sr-only text, chip labels inject raw MEDIA_ICONS SVG strings via dangerouslySetInnerHTML (line 62, mapExplorerFormat.ts:30-34) with no ARIA, and the Nearest Targets sidebar rows (MapExplorer.tsx:1315-1319) render only name/location/distance — missingTypes never appears as text on any keyboard/SR path. The type-filter pills filter the set but don't convey per-target info, so the feature's core information is icon-only, contradicting ACCESSIBILITY.md line 19's hidden-label claim. Moderate is the right severity: SR users can reach targets but lose the missing-media detail.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested fix is right; extend it slightly: also add aria-hidden="true" into the three MEDIA_ICONS SVG strings in lib/mapExplorerFormat.ts so browse-mode screen readers don't hit unnamed images on the on-map chips, and for the sidebar rows reuse the existing sr-only span pattern already used for the recency dot at MapExplorer.tsx:1311-1313 (e.g. Missing photo, audio).

title: 'Nearest Targets' list is not scoped to the map view and does not update on pan/zoom, contrary to the statement
description: ACCESSIBILITY.md says the Media Targets mode's 'Nearest Targets' list 'works the same way' as the in-view lists and then asserts 'These lists are scoped to the current map view and update as you pan or zoom (very dense views are capped, with a "zoom in to narrow the list" hint).' The keyboard path itself is real (each row has a focusable, aria-labelled locate button at lines 1320-1333 that opens the same popup and pans). But `nearest10` (lines 453-461) is computed as the 10 closest pins to the SEARCH CENTER lat/lng inputs — it ignores `mapBounds`, never reacts to panning or zooming, and has no over-cap hint. Only the 'Sightings in view' and 'Hotspots in view' lists (markersInView + mapBounds, cap 200, MapSidebarUI.tsx:118-121) match the published description. A screen-reader user following the statement would expect the targets keyboard list to track the viewport; it doesn't.
fix: Either scope the targets list with markersInView(displayedTargetPins, mapBounds) like the other two lists, or correct ACCESSIBILITY.md to say the targets list is the 10 nearest to the search center.

verdict.reasoning: nearest10 (MapExplorer.tsx:453-461) is sorted by distance from the lat/lng search-center inputs with deps [displayedTargetPins, lat, lng] — it never reads mapBounds, never reacts to pan/zoom, and has no over-cap hint — while ACCESSIBILITY.md line 13 explicitly includes the Nearest Targets list in 'These lists are scoped to the current map view and update as you pan or zoom'. The gap is functional, not just a claims bug: target chips are DOM divs with onClick but no tabIndex (TargetMarkers.tsx), so targets beyond the 10 nearest to the center have no keyboard path at all while mouse users can click any chip. Moderate is fair (false published assistive-behavior claim plus a real 2.1.1 gap).
verdict.fixNote: If scoping to the viewport, reuse the existing pattern rather than patching nearest10: derive markersInView(displayedTargetPins, mapBounds) and render through the shared InViewMarkerList (MapSidebarUI.tsx) like sightingsInView/hotspotsInView, which gives the cap + 'zoom in to narrow the list' hint for free. Otherwise the one-line ACCESSIBILITY.md correction ('the targets list shows the 10 nearest the search center') is the cheaper honest fix.

title: List Comparer summary bars and result panels don't reflow at 320px — labels truncate to identical text
description: Both comparer results screens use rigid column counts with no narrow-width collapse. The five-cell summary (`gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(5, 1fr)'` — ResultsView.tsx:111 and ChecklistComparer.tsx:281) gives each cell ~58px at 320px; the 0.625rem uppercase labels are `whiteSpace: nowrap; overflow: hidden; textOverflow: ellipsis` (ResultsView.tsx:165-173, ChecklistComparer.tsx:478), so "Checklist A" and "Checklist B" (and "<name> total" pairs) ellipsize to identical strings — the numbers become indistinguishable at that width. Below them, ResultsView.tsx:129 `repeat(3, 1fr)` species panels and ChecklistComparer.tsx:310 `1fr 1fr` A-only/B-only panels never stack, leaving ~90-140px columns where species names wrap to 4+ lines. Nothing scrolls two-dimensionally and the panel headers repeat the counts, so it is degraded rather than lost — but the summary labels' ambiguity is a concrete information loss at 320px.
fix: Use `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(7rem, 1fr))` for the stat bars (cells wrap to two rows on narrow screens), and collapse the panel grids to one column under 640px (reuse the `.sr-two-col` media-query pattern from globals.css:601).

verdict.reasoning: Verified all cited lines: ResultsView.tsx:111 `repeat(5, 1fr)` with nowrap/ellipsis 0.625rem labels (165-176), :129 `repeat(3, 1fr)` panels, and the ChecklistComparer twins (281, 310, ~479) — all inline styles with zero responsive handling (no matchMedia, no media-query class) anywhere in ResultsView/ListComparer/ChecklistComparer. At 320px each stat cell is ~55-64px with 40px horizontal padding, leaving ~15-24px for the label (1-3 chars + ellipsis): 'Checklist A'/'Checklist B' and filename-derived labels (eBird exports share the 'MyEBirdData' prefix) truncate to identical strings — concrete information loss under SC 1.4.10, though the both/A-only/B-only counts are duplicated in the panel headers so only the two totals become truly ambiguous. Moderate is the right severity: real AA failure at 320px/400% zoom, but degraded rather than blocking.
verdict.fixNote: The stats-bar half of the fix is sound (rem-based `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(7rem, 1fr))` inline also scales with the in-app Text Size control). The panel half won't work as written: the grids' `gridTemplateColumns` are inline styles, and a media-query class rule cannot override an inline declaration — move the grid definition into a class (as SpeciesDetail.tsx:802 uses `className="sr-two-col"` with no inline grid). ResultsView's panel grid is 3 columns, so `.sr-two-col` isn't directly reusable: either add an `.sr-compare-panels { grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr) }` base rule with a `1fr` override in the existing `@media (max-width: 640px)` block in globals.css (the ChecklistComparer's 1fr-1fr grid CAN reuse `.sr-two-col` directly), or skip media queries entirely with inline `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(14rem, 1fr))`. Also note ACCESSIBILITY.md line 39 currently claims narrow-window reflow 'without clipping content' — it should be corrected or the fix shipped to keep that published statement true.

title: Tab Layout reordering is mouse/touch-only with no keyboard alternative — the statement's keyboard section discloses no exceptions
wcag: 2.1.1 Keyboard A (also WCAG 2.2 2.5.7 Dragging Movements AA)
description: Settings → Tab Layout reorders tabs exclusively via HTML5 drag-and-drop on the <li> rows; the 'drag handle' is a non-focusable plain <div> carrying an aria-label (which is also invalid ARIA on a generic div — it won't be announced), and there is no keyboard mechanism (no move-up/move-down buttons, no arrow-key handling). The app itself admits this in an sr-only note at Settings.tsx:699 ('Keyboard reordering is not supported in this version'), and ACCESSIBILITY.md's 'Nearly all of SnowRaven is reachable and operable with the keyboard alone' hedge technically covers it — but the Keyboard Navigation section enumerates zero exceptions, so a reader has no way to learn this feature is keyboard-inaccessible. Show/hide toggles are keyboard-accessible; ordering is not achievable at all without a pointer, which is a hard 2.1.1 failure for that function (and a 2.5.7 Dragging Movements failure under WCAG 2.2).
fix: Add keyboard reordering (focusable handle button with ArrowUp/ArrowDown + aria-live position announcements, or per-row Move up/Move down buttons), and until then name this exception explicitly in ACCESSIBILITY.md's keyboard section.

verdict.reasoning: Both halves check out: (a) reordering is pointer-only — DnD on the <li>, unfocusable handle div with an invalid aria-label, no keyboard mechanism in the file — and (b) ACCESSIBILITY.md's Keyboard Navigation section enumerates only the map-marker caveat and never names this exception, so the 'Nearly all' hedge gives readers no way to learn ordering is keyboard-inaccessible. The sr-only in-app note (line 699) is disclosure to SR users but not in the published statement, so alreadyDisclosed stays false. Moderate is fair for the claims-dimension framing (the underlying 2.1.1 failure is index 3's serious finding); the fix — keyboard reorder, or naming the exception in ACCESSIBILITY.md until then — is correct.

title: DOM map markers (Species Detail / Named Birds pins, target chips, Statistics rank pins) are unnamed, role-less click targets invisible to AT
wcag: 1.1.1 Non-text Content A / 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value A
description: ACCESSIBILITY.md documents sidebar-list alternatives for the Map Explorer's GPU canvas markers, but the DOM <Marker> maps have no equivalent treatment: SightingsMap.tsx:55-58 renders each pin as a clickable <div> containing an innerHTML SVG with no role, name, or tabindex; TargetMarkers.tsx:69-74 does the same for target chips; BirdingStats.tsx:863-872 for the Statistics RankIcon pins (statsPrimitives.tsx:92-101, an unnamed SVG). Screen-reader and keyboard users cannot perceive or activate any of these markers or reach their popups. Impact is moderated because equivalent data exists in adjacent text on most surfaces (Named Birds rows list every sighting date/location/checklist; Species Detail has Top Locations and per-sighting lists; Statistics has top-location tables), but the popup-only details (e.g. per-coordinate date groupings) have no named path.
fix: Make the Marker child a real button: role="button", tabIndex=0, aria-label like `${locName ?? coordinate}, ${sightings.length} sightings` with Enter/Space handling — or explicitly scope the ACCESSIBILITY.md marker claim and guarantee a text equivalent exists beside every DOM-marker map.

verdict.reasoning: The literal 'no role, name' claim is partly wrong — maplibre 5.24's Marker.addTo() (src/ui/marker.ts:340-348) stamps every marker wrapper with role='button' and default aria-label='Map marker' — but the substantive 1.1.1 failure stands: all pins announce identically with no location/count, are not focusable (tabindex comes only from the unused setPopup path), and the popup-only per-coordinate details have no named path. The cited mitigations are real (BirdingStats pins duplicate the adjacent 'Top locations by checklists/species' lists; NamedBirdRow lists every checklist link; TargetMarkers has the Nearest Targets sidebar), so moderate is the right severity. ACCESSIBILITY.md's marker claim is Map Explorer-only and does not disclose this.
verdict.fixNote: Correction to the finding's mechanism: the markers are not role-less/invisible — maplibre already applies role='button' + a generic identical aria-label ('Map marker') to the wrapper, so the defect is a non-descriptive name plus no focusability. Fix by giving each pin a descriptive per-pin name: either set it on the wrapper via the Marker ref (marker.getElement().setAttribute('aria-label', `${locName ?? coord}, ${n} sightings`) plus tabindex='0' — maplibre preserves a pre-set label), or render a real <button aria-label=...> child and demote the wrapper to role='presentation' via the ref to avoid nested-button announcements. The finding's hand-rolled role='button'/tabIndex/Enter-Space div is workable but creates button-inside-button nesting and re-implements what a native <button> gives for free.

title: Collapsed dropdown nav orphans every tabpanel (dangling aria-labelledby, no tablist)
description: All panels in App.tsx use aria-labelledby="tab-{id}" (e.g. App.tsx:590). In the collapsed TabDropdown mode the id="tab-{id}" elements exist only on the listbox options while the menu is open (TabNav.tsx:298) — with the menu closed (the normal state) the visible role="tabpanel" references a nonexistent id and there is no tablist/tab anywhere in the tree, so the tab/tabpanel relationship ACCESSIBILITY.md claims ("Tabs and their panels are linked with the correct tab/tabpanel roles") is broken precisely for the zoom/narrow-viewport users who get the dropdown. The dropdown also replaces tab semantics with listbox semantics, leaving orphaned tabpanels.
fix: Give panels a stable label that doesn't depend on the bar variant — e.g. aria-label={TAB_LABELS[id]} on each panel (or keep aria-labelledby but render persistent visually-hidden label elements), and use distinct ids for dropdown options.

verdict.reasoning: All ten App.tsx panels (lines 588-1073) use role=tabpanel + aria-labelledby="tab-{id}", but in collapsed mode the only tab-{id} elements are dropdown options (TabNav.tsx:298) that exist only while the menu is open and carry role=option, not role=tab — so in the normal closed state every labelledby idref dangles and the tabpanels are orphaned with no tablist in the tree. ACCESSIBILITY.md line 19 explicitly claims 'Tabs and their panels are linked with the correct tab/tabpanel roles' and its only disclosed contrast/structure exception is chart-bar labels, so this contradicts a published statement rather than being disclosed. Moderate is fair: it breaks panel names and structure for the entire narrow-viewport/zoom audience.

title: ToggleSwitch off-state track is nearly invisible in light theme (1.48:1)
description: The off-state track uses --sr-gray-400 (#D4D4D8): 1.48:1 against the white button surface AND 1.48:1 against the white knob, so the knob position — the visual state indicator of every 'merge subspecies' / 'show spuh' / 'hide weather' switch — is barely discernible in light theme (the on state passes: accent track 4.52:1 vs surface). Dark theme: track vs surface 2.29:1 (also <3:1) though knob-vs-track passes (7.73:1). aria-checked is correct for AT, but the sighted off/on distinction fails non-text contrast.
fix: Darken the light off-track (e.g. #8E8E96 ≈ 3.1:1 on white and vs the white knob) and lighten the dark off-track (e.g. #6E6E78), or add a 1px --sr-border-medium-darkened outline to the track and knob.

verdict.reasoning: Independently recomputed all ratios from globals.css tokens and they match exactly: light off-track #D4D4D8 is 1.48:1 vs both the white surface and the white knob (knob position imperceptible), on-track 4.52:1, dark track 2.29:1 vs surface with knob-vs-track 7.73:1. ACCESSIBILITY.md claims form controls meet AA contrast and discloses only chart-bar labels, so this is not a known exception. Moderate is right: a genuine 1.4.11 failure on a widely-used control, but state remains inferable from green-present/absent (state-vs-state 3.06:1) and aria-checked is correct for AT.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested hexes verify (#8E8E96 = 3.25:1 on white; #6E6E78 = 3.51:1 vs dark surface, 5.04:1 vs white knob), but '--sr-border-medium-darkened' does not exist and hardcoded hexes in the component would violate the --sr-* token rule. Since --sr-gray-400 has no other consumers, either retune --sr-gray-400 to #8E8E96 (:root) / #6E6E78 ([data-theme="dark"]) in frontend/src/globals.css, or — cleaner, since #8E8E96 would be oddly dark for a 'gray-400' slot — add a dedicated --sr-toggle-off-track token in BOTH themes and reference it at ToggleSwitch.tsx:27. Also update the ACCESSIBILITY.md contrast claim if the fix doesn't ship immediately.

title: WelcomeScreen modal has no focus trap; map fullscreen overlay leaves hidden chrome tabbable
description: WelcomeScreen declares role="dialog" aria-modal="true" and handles only Escape (line 21) — there is no Tab containment and the app behind it is not inert, so tabbing past "Explore the app first" moves focus into the fully obscured app underneath (the overlay background is opaque var(--sr-bg)); a sighted keyboard user loses the focus indicator entirely while aria-modal simultaneously tells screen readers the background doesn't exist. The map fullscreen mode has the same background-tabbing issue: it is a CSS overlay (panel fixed inset 0, App.tsx:1031-1042) and only body scroll is locked (App.tsx:390-395), so the tab bar and footer remain in the tab order while visually covered. (Not a 2.1.2 trap — focus can always leave — but focus lands on invisible controls.)
fix: Give WelcomeScreen the same Tab-wrap handler HelpDocs uses (HelpDocs.tsx:256-274). For map fullscreen, set inert (or aria-hidden + tabindex management) on the sibling app chrome while active, and consider Escape-to-exit-fullscreen as polish.

verdict.reasoning: WelcomeScreen.tsx:19-24 handles only Escape with no Tab containment while declaring aria-modal="true", and App.tsx:1195-1201 mounts it inside the full app tree, so the obscured tab bar/footer remain tabbable behind the opaque var(--sr-bg) overlay. The map fullscreen claim also holds: App.tsx:1031-1033 is a fixed inset-0 z-1200 CSS overlay and App.tsx:389-395 locks only body scroll — no inert/aria-hidden/focus-trap exists anywhere in frontend/src. ACCESSIBILITY.md's Focus Management section discloses only the Map Explorer filter-panel trap, not this gap; moderate is the right severity (focus lands on invisible controls but is recoverable, not a 2.1.2 trap).
verdict.fixNote: The suggested fix is correct and convention-consistent — HelpDocs.tsx:258-274 has exactly the referenced Tab-wrap handler. Two refinements: WelcomeScreen should query focusables from a ref on its own root div (it has no DOM id, unlike HelpDocs' getElementById('sr-help-overlay')), and for map fullscreen the `inert` attribute is safe in both desktop targets (WKWebView/Safari 15.5+, WebView2) — apply it to the sibling tabpanels, TabNav, and footer while mapFullscreen && activeTab === 'map-explorer', clearing it in the same effect cleanup as the existing body scroll lock at App.tsx:390-395. Update ACCESSIBILITY.md's Focus Management section in the same change per CLAUDE.md.

title: Multi-series line charts differentiated by hue alone
description: The media-over-time chart draws four lines (photo/audio/video/total) distinguished only by stroke color, with a color-keyed legend — for color-blind users the photo (blue) vs video (purple) pair in particular is hard to separate. Tooltips name each series on hover and the role="img" summary covers AT users, so the information is reachable, but not glanceable. Same pattern wherever SightingsGraph's media chart overlays multiple series.
fix: Add per-series strokeDasharray patterns and/or distinct dot marker shapes to the recharts <Line> elements so series differ by more than hue.

verdict.reasoning: Lines 1775-1778 of BirdingStats.tsx render four <Line> series with dot={false}, no strokeDasharray, and only stroke color differentiating them; Vienot protan/deutan simulation collapses the photo #3B82F6 / video #8B5CF6 pair from RGB distance 88.6 to ~1-2 (same in dark theme #60A5FA/#A78BFA), confirming the confusion claim. SightingsGraph.tsx's media overlay (lines ~157-172) is likewise hue-only (its dots are same-shape circles in the series color). Hover tooltips and the role=img label keep the info reachable, so minor severity is correctly stated.
verdict.fixNote: Add per-series strokeDasharray to the four <Line>s in BirdingStats.tsx (e.g. photo solid, audio '6 3', video '2 3', total '8 3 2 3'); since dot={false} there, dashes are the practical cue. Apply the same patterns to the photo/audio/video overlay in speciesDetail/SightingsGraph.tsx (~lines 157-172). Note recharts' default Legend line icon does not render the dash pattern, so either pass a custom legend `content` or distinct `legendType` icons so the legend also differs by more than hue. Also note ACCESSIBILITY.md currently claims 'Color is never the only way information is conveyed' — update it (or fix the charts in the same change) per the CLAUDE.md rule that it must stay true.

title: Chart non-text elements below 3:1: amber line in light theme, faint bar segments, stacked-segment boundaries
description: Computed non-text chart parts under 3:1 — light theme: the Audio series line --sr-graph-audio #F59E0B vs the white card = 2.15:1 (media-over-time chart; SightingsGraph media line too), --sr-chart-blue-light bar segment vs surface = 1.80:1, tier-1 fill vs surface = 2.64:1; the hand-built stacked breeding bar's adjacent segments: tier-2 vs tier-1 = 2.04:1 light / 1.50:1 dark, tier-4 vs tier-2 = 2.79:1 light / 2.20:1 dark (BirdingStats.tsx:1677-1679). Mitigations keeping this minor: every chart has a data-bearing role="img" label, tooltips, and most values are duplicated as text (legend counts, BarRow numerals).
fix: Darken light --sr-graph-audio toward #B45309 (5.02:1 — already proven in --sr-age-immature), add 1px separators between stacked-bar segments, and bump light --sr-chart-blue-light/tier-1 fills toward their 3:1 neighbors.

verdict.reasoning: Recomputed all cited non-text ratios and they match: light --sr-graph-audio #F59E0B vs white 2.15:1 (media LineChart at :1776), --sr-chart-blue-light vs white 1.80:1, tier-1 vs white 2.64:1, and the hand-built stacked breeding bar's adjacent segments at :1677-1679 (tier-2/tier-1 2.04 light / 1.50 dark; tier-4/tier-2 2.79 / 2.20). The stated mitigations are real (role="img" summaries at :557/:1266/:1755, legends, BarRow prints value+pct as text), which correctly keeps this at minor under 1.4.11's redundant-presentation allowance — the amber series line is the strongest genuine instance since the lines themselves carry the trend.
verdict.fixNote: Darkening light --sr-graph-audio toward #B45309 (5.02:1, matches light --sr-age-immature) is verified and safe. But do NOT shift the shared --sr-tier-* palette to fix the stacked-bar boundaries — those tokens drive the map atlas overlay, hatch sprites (--sr-tier-N-rgb), legend parity, and the breeding-badge dark-text-on-light-tier pairing called out in ACCESSIBILITY.md; instead add 1px var(--sr-surface) gaps between the three stacked segments at BirdingStats.tsx:1677-1679, which fixes segment distinguishability with zero blast radius.

title: Recency tier is color-alone at a glance (sighted users); the faint 'old' dot compounds it in light theme (1.64:1)
description: The fresh/mid/old recency tiers on the Nearest Targets sidebar dots and the on-map chip backgrounds are differentiated only by color for sighted users; the sr-only labels (MapExplorer.tsx:1311-1313) cover screen readers — so ACCESSIBILITY.md's specific claim about hidden labels on recency dots is TRUE — and the popup shows the tier as text ('≤7 days') plus the date, so the information is reachable by interaction. But a color-blind user scanning the list/map cannot rank targets without clicking each one, and the light-theme 'old' dot (#A8D4BB) is also only 1.64:1 against the sidebar surface (its compensating border is --sr-border at 1.27:1).
fix: Show the visible date (already computed) or a tier letter/shape next to each sidebar dot, and give the 'old' dot a ≥3:1 border (e.g. --sr-accent-strong).

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran the WCAG math: light-theme --sr-map-target-old #A8D4BB vs the sidebar's var(--sr-surface) #FFFFFF is 1.64:1 and the dot's --sr-border #E4E4E7 border is 1.27:1 — the reported ratios are exact (the 'old' tier takes the var(--sr-border) border branch at :1310 since its text token isn't 'white'). The sidebar row (:1310-1319) shows name/location/distance but no date or tier text, and the on-map chips (TargetMarkers.tsx) are colored by tier only, so the tier IS color-alone at a glance for sighted users; the sr-only labels (:1311-1313) and the popup's '≤7 days' text + date exist as the finding accurately concedes. Minor is fair given the interaction path, and the fix is valid: --sr-accent-strong exists in both themes (globals.css:30/:131) and is 7.98:1 against the light surface.

title: Bird-name links replace the standard focus ring with only a color change + underline
wcag: 2.4.7 Focus Visible AA (weak indicator; 2.4.13 Focus Appearance fail forward-looking)
description: `.sr-birdname-link:hover, .sr-birdname-link:focus-visible { color: var(--sr-accent); text-decoration: underline; outline: none; }` — the class rule out-specifies the global `button:focus-visible` outline, so the most common interactive element in the app (every species name in Life List, Breeding Codes, Checklists, Map Explorer, Statistics, comparer rows) shows only a green tint + underline on keyboard focus, identical to the mouse hover style. In a dense table of hundreds of rows this is materially harder to track than the 3px ring used everywhere else, and it weakens the ACCESSIBILITY.md claim of a 'clear green outline' wherever focus lands. The global rule's faint 12% box-shadow still applies but contributes almost nothing.
fix: Split the selector: keep `outline: none` for :hover only, and let :focus-visible keep (or restore) the global outline alongside the color/underline — e.g. `.sr-birdname-link:focus-visible { color: var(--sr-accent); text-decoration: underline; }` with no outline override.

verdict.reasoning: Rule verified verbatim at globals.css:306; BirdName renders a <button class="sr-birdname-link"> with no other focus styling, and the (0,2,0) class selector beats the (0,1,1) global button:focus-visible ring, leaving only color+underline plus the near-invisible 12%-alpha box-shadow. However keyboard focus still produces a clearly visible change (4.18:1 color shift plus an underline appearing), so WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.7 technically passes and 2.4.13 Focus Appearance is AAA in WCAG 2.2 — this is a real consistency issue that also contradicts ACCESSIBILITY.md's 'clear green outline' claim, but not an AA failure, so moderate overstates it.
verdict.fixNote: No selector split needed: just delete `outline: none` from the combined rule — `.sr-birdname-link:hover, .sr-birdname-link:focus-visible { color: var(--sr-accent); text-decoration: underline; }`. Hover never paints an outline on a non-focused element, and the suggested split's `:hover { outline: none }` would suppress the ring whenever a focused name is also hovered; with the override gone, the global `button:focus-visible` 3px ring applies on keyboard focus only.

title: Inline `outline: 'none'` on ~20 inputs/selects suppresses the designed focus ring app-wide
description: One repeated pattern: form controls styled with inline `outline: 'none'`, which overrides the global input ring (globals.css:556-563, `outline: 2px solid var(--sr-accent)`). The only surviving indicator is the rule's `border-color: var(--sr-accent) !important` (stylesheet !important still beats inline) plus a 12%-alpha shadow — a 1.5px gray→green border tint instead of the designed 2px ring, easy to miss in dense filter sidebars, and weaker than ACCESSIBILITY.md's published 'border-hugging ring on inputs'. Locations: lib/mapExplorerFormat.ts:27 (SELECT_STYLE shared by all Map Explorer selects); MapExplorer.tsx:88,690,692,863,865,1184; LifeList.tsx:627,653,667; BreedingCodeList.tsx:388,419,435; SpeciesDetail.tsx:518,613,638,652,1273; Checklists.tsx:170,265; MediaCommentsSection.tsx:75; Settings.tsx:435,1219,1231,1243. Technically still a visible state change (so not a hard 2.4.7 fail), but a significant app-wide degradation versus the global design.
fix: Remove every inline `outline: 'none'` from inputs/selects — the global stylesheet already suppresses the default ring on non-focus-visible states and supplies the 2px accent ring on focus. The per-element onFocus borderColor handlers (e.g. Settings.tsx:437) become redundant and can stay or go.

verdict.reasoning: Verified all claims: 26 inline outline:'none' occurrences match the listed locations, inline style beats the non-!important outline in globals.css:556-563, and only the !important border-color plus the stylesheet box-shadow survive — the designed 2px ring never renders on these controls. However the surviving indicator (1.5px border flipping gray→accent at 4.52:1 light / 9.22:1 dark vs surface, plus a 4px glow, with explicit onFocus borderColor handlers in Settings) is a perceivable, conventional focus treatment, so 2.4.7 AA is not actually failed — the finding itself concedes this. Real as an app-wide design-consistency issue that also makes ACCESSIBILITY.md's published 'border-hugging ring on inputs' claim inaccurate, but a non-failing degradation grades as minor, not moderate.

title: Desktop: no page-zoom path exists — Ctrl/Cmd+= is a no-op and the window floor is 800 CSS px, so the 1.4.10 reflow condition is unreachable and ACCESSIBILITY.md's zoom sentence is false on desktop
wcag: 1.4.10 Reflow AA (WCAG2ICT) / 1.4.4 Resize Text AA — plus published-claim accuracy
description: The main window sets minWidth: 800 (tauri.conf.json:17) and does NOT set zoomHotkeysEnabled, which defaults to false (verified in the repo's own @tauri-apps/cli config.schema.json: WindowConfig.zoomHotkeysEnabled, "default": false — on Windows it controls WebView2's IsZoomControlEnabled, i.e. Ctrl+hotkey AND Ctrl+wheel zoom; on macOS/Linux it injects a JS polyfill). No Rust code wires any menu, accelerator, or zoom command (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:48-68 registers only plugins and 5 commands; main.rs is 6 lines), and capabilities/default.json lacks the webview:allow-set-webview-zoom permission the macOS/Linux polyfill would require even if enabled. Net effect, derived statically: in the desktop app, Ctrl/Cmd +/−/wheel zoom does nothing on any platform, and the window can never present narrower than 800 CSS px. Consequences under WCAG2ICT reasoning: (1) the web audit's 1.4.10 verification at 320 CSS px and its 1.4.4 verification via browser zoom are both unreachable on desktop — the only enlargement mechanism is the in-app Text Size control capped at 200% (lib/textScale.ts:11, TEXT_SCALES max 2). That satisfies SC 1.4.4's 200% requirement, but the 400%-equivalent enlarged view SC 1.4.10 presupposes (1280px viewport at 400% = 320 CSS px) can never be produced, so the desktop product conforms to 1.4.10 only vacuously, and a desktop low-vision user who needs more than 2x enlargement has no in-app path at all (a web user has browser zoom to 400%+, stackable with Text Size). OS display scaling enlarges physical pixels but cannot push the window below 800 CSS px either. (2) ACCESSIBILITY.md:39 states "Browser/page zoom (Ctrl/Cmd +/−) works too" within a statement that explicitly covers the desktop app (line 3: "It runs in the browser and as a desktop app") — that sentence is false on desktop, and it sits two lines below line 37's own correct disclosure that the desktop app "has no browser zoom of its own", an internal contradiction. Status: the config default is documented and there is zero zoom wiring anywhere in src-tauri, so this is asserted statically; a live desktop run to confirm the hotkeys are inert is advisable (needs-runtime-verification as a formality only).
evidence: tauri.conf.json:12-19 window config contains only title/width/height/minWidth/minHeight; node_modules/@tauri-apps/cli/config.schema.json WindowConfig.zoomHotkeysEnabled → "default": false, macOS/Linux polyfill "Requires `webview:allow-set-webview-zoom` permission"; src-tauri/capabilities/default.json has no webview:* permission; ACCESSIBILITY.md:39 "Browser/page zoom (Ctrl/Cmd +/−) works too." vs :37 "the desktop app, which has no browser zoom of its own".
suggestedFix: Set "zoomHotkeysEnabled": true on the main window in tauri.conf.json and add "webview:allow-set-webview-zoom" to capabilities/default.json — Tauri then provides Ctrl/Cmd +/− page zoom from 20% to 1000% on all three desktop platforms, giving the desktop product a real 1.4.10/1.4.4 path (verify on a live build, especially the macOS/Linux polyfill). Independently and immediately, reword ACCESSIBILITY.md line 39 to scope the page-zoom sentence to the browser build (e.g. "In the browser, page zoom (Ctrl/Cmd +/−) works too") so the published statement is true for desktop, and update it again when the hotkeys ship.

verdict.reasoning: Every static claim verified: tauri.conf.json:17 sets minWidth 800 with no zoomHotkeysEnabled (schema default false, macOS/Linux polyfill needs webview:allow-set-webview-zoom which capabilities/default.json lacks), src-tauri/src/lib.rs wires no zoom, and TEXT_SCALES caps at 2 — so the desktop app genuinely offers no enlargement beyond 200% and no path to a 320-CSS-px-equivalent view. But no WCAG 2.1 AA SC is actually failed: 1.4.4 is satisfied by the 200% Text Size control and 1.4.10 is vacuously met (the condition is unreachable, not violated), and ACCESSIBILITY.md:37 itself already discloses the desktop app 'has no browser zoom of its own', leaving only line 39's ambiguous sentence as the doc defect. Real and worth fixing (cheap config change, genuine benefit to low-vision desktop users needing >2x), but moderate overstates a beyond-AA gap; minor.
